findings.title: Specify a transport that can persist the supported Studio document size
findings.trigger: Commit a valid Studio document larger than the existing 2 MiB command-envelope limit, within the planned 8 MiB document scope.
findings.evidence: The proposed commit takes inline document content. Current HTTP commands are bounded by requestBytes=2 MiB; Studio permits 8 MiB, and JSON string escaping can enlarge wire bytes further. Moving document bytes out of the snapshot does not resolve ingress.
findings.impact: Cursor must invent a new publication protocol or silently reduce a supported canvas size; the first persistence slice cannot meet the stated boundary as specified.
findings.repair: Specify bounded authenticated document staging and an immutable server-issued handle/hash consumed by the revision-bound commit, including abandoned-upload GC and project ownership; alternatively explicitly reduce the supported serialized wire size and show a safe refusal. Keep global command limits unless a separately reviewed policy change is intended.
findings.acceptance: Browser/REST/MCP/SDK tests cover just below/at/above both wire and document byte bounds, multibyte/escaped text, replay, foreign handle, abandoned stage and crash-before-attach; no acknowledged document is lost.

findings.title: Gate writable v5 promotion on lossless existing edit paths and complete recovery
findings.trigger: A Studio/Cinema persistence task is merged and promoted before YU-014/YU-015; an ordinary timeline/full-project save or undo then runs against a document-bearing v5 project.
findings.evidence: The graph permits individual persistence tasks to become VERIFIED before complete recovery and browser command cohesion. Current #commit rebuilds canonical state from the editing projection; those conversion functions currently enumerate only known fields, and non-edit-history operations clear the edit chain. The new plan needs an explicit preservation/activation contract for these paths.
findings.impact: A locally passing document commit could be presented as durable persistence while another existing mutation drops its references or recovery/undo remains incomplete.
findings.repair: Define a shared activation gate for live writable-v5/default UI promotion, separate from build dependencies to avoid a cycle. Require all existing mutation/projection/undo paths to preserve creative references server-side where safe, otherwise reject a lossy save. Individual task verification may cover a flag-off contract but must state activation is still blocked.
findings.acceptance: Create canvas/scene/story refs, perform existing save/rename/timeline edits and writer-scoped undo/redo including old-client/lost-response/concurrent-writer cases, kill/reopen, backup/restore and verify exact document/media closure before activation.

findings.title: Separate optional transform animation from the independent complexity fix
findings.evidence: YU-022 depends only on YU-019 but mentions adding transform channels after YU-020 parity. The conditional prose is stricter than the machine graph for that optional sub-scope.
findings.repair: Keep YU-022 limited to existing opacity/volume compilation, with transform animation a child task depending on YU-020 and YU-022; or encode the conditional sub-scope explicitly in task selection/receipts.
findings.impact: Avoid an implementation agent broadening a performance fix into unqualified effect channels.

findings.title: Freeze a smaller audience and journey before expanding the ten-phase roadmap
findings.evidence: The first integrity slice is credibly separated, but the broader product still spans editor, canvas, cinematic previs, consent/identity, agents, captions, interchange and engines without observed target-user task evidence.
findings.repair: After integrity qualification, freeze one bilingual short-film finishing brief and a small formative study as the next prioritization checkpoint; permit reordering or deferring later work based on observed completion failures.
findings.impact: Reduce solo-founder maintenance scope and validate that the selected workspace structure improves a real creator journey.

findings.title: Do not treat missing generation benchmarks or exhaustive donor qualification as concealed passes
findings.evidence: The package explicitly labels head-to-head results NOT TESTED, separates pilot from powered comparisons, clusters repeated prompt/rater evidence, retains failures, and states source/runtime/resource gaps under PARTIALLY READY.
findings.disposition: These limitations restrict future claims and activation; they are not grounds to demand paid/model work now or to call the existing plan a release approval.

findings.title: Do not require a native editor rewrite from the current architecture comparison
findings.evidence: Scores are labeled engineering judgment, include migration/maintenance sensitivity and explicit falsifiers, while native preview adoption requires a matched Windows lifecycle/parity spike.
findings.disposition: Preserving the existing authority and testing the narrower route first is defensible under the verified zero-spend/unqualified-GPU constraints.

limitations: Planning review only. The two must-fixes concern implementation handoff and promotion conditions, not a claim that unimplemented production code has already failed.
